summary: IdP emitted JSON-blob attribute causes RBAC role desync during console login
summary_short: Intermittent logins succeed but user roles are empty after IdP attribute change
description:
Issue summary: After a routine IdP metadata update at customer identity provider (partner IdP), a subset of internal users report successful console login but do not receive any RBAC roles (403 when accessing modelobservability and runbook tools). Impact: Blocks developers and oncall engineers from running elevated commands and accessing dashboards. Incident first observed ~2026-03-10 09:12 UTC for ~12 users across multiple teams.

Observed behavior: Authentication (SAML/OIDC handshake) completes and session cookie is issued. Console shows "Signed in" but requests for protected pages return 403. The user session contains an authenticated subject but roles claim is empty.

Expected behavior: Roles derived from group claims in the IdP assertion are populated and RBAC grants appropriate permissions.

Affected scope: ~12 users (internal), intermittent pattern depending on which upstream SP/IdP connector the user hit; primarily users whose Okta profiles contain a new attribute named `x-org-attributes` which is a JSON blob (array) rather than the flat list of group DNs our claim parser expects.

Steps to reproduce: 
1) Use Okta account with `x-org-attributes` set to a JSON array string (example payload attached).
2) SSO to console via SAML redirect flow.
3) Observe successful sign-in and session cookie creation.
4) Visit /modelobservability or /runbooks -> receive 403 and UI shows no roles.

Logs/artifacts: 
- Example SAML assertion (sanitized) attached in ticket comment.
- Identity-proxy logs show claim "x-org-attributes" present and passed through as a single string value.
- RBAC evaluator logs: "no roles found for subject uid=ajenkins@redwood.ai" and downstream mapping aborted due to parse error: "unexpected token '{' at position 0".

Impact: Productivity blocked for impacted engineers; additional friction for oncall rotations when roleless sessions are issued. Severity flagged Sev1 due to direct operational impact for internal tooling access.

Initial hypothesis: Recent upstream IdP schema change turned group attributes into a JSON string blob for richer metadata; our claim normalization pipeline assumed a comma-separated string or multiple claim occurrences and does not parse JSON blobs. The identity-proxy treats the entire blob as a single claim value, leading to RBAC mapping failure.

Note: This is not a network/TLS issue, nor a token expiry problem. The issue happens immediately after login if the user has the new attribute format.
steps_to_reproduce: Initiate SAML SSO to console in prod-us-east
Observe session cookie set, then visit protected page returns 403
Inspect identity-proxy logs for claim pass-through and RBAC evaluator logs for parse errors
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Auth team reproduced locally using a synthetic assertion where groups claim is a JSON array string. Identity-proxy V2 forwarder passes claim as-is to RBAC service. 2026-03-10 13:40 UTC - Deployed temporary parsing shim on staging identity-proxy that stringify-parses JSON blobs into multiple group claims; RBAC mapping then succeeds in staging. Related PR open to add robust claim normalization in identity-proxy: github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/486. We are also tracking a notification from partner IdP indicating the attribute format change (internal thread: #identity-updates).
logs_excerpt:
[identity-proxy] 2026-03-10T09:15:23Z INFO received assertion subject=ajenkins@redwood.ai claims={"x-org-attributes":"[{\"org\":\"infra\",\"role\":\"oncall\"}]"}
[rbac] 2026-03-10T09:15:23Z ERROR failed to map roles for subject=ajenkins@redwood.ai error="json parse error: unexpected token '{'"
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-10 09:28: Logged initial user reports and attached sanitized SAML assertion. Notified identity and auth owners.
Tom Chen (assignee) - 2026-03-10 10:07: Reproduced issue locally and added a minimal parsing shim in staging. Raising P1; planning quick fix in identity-proxy to normalize claim formats.
SRE - 2026-03-10 11:22: Verified no network faults; sessions are healthy and cookies set with expected attributes. Confirmed RBAC evaluator receives raw claim value that contains JSON blob.
Security - 2026-03-10 12:05: Approved temporary staging shim for rapid verification; emphasized no sensitive attributes should be logged.
Tom Chen - 2026-03-11 09:30: Rolled out parsing shim to a single proxy shard in prod-us-east for canary. 3 of 12 affected users can now access tooling normally. Monitoring for regressions.
hypothesis: Identity provider started packing group metadata into a single JSON-encoded attribute; our claim normalization fails to split/parse that blob into discrete group values, causing RBAC to find zero groups and drop roles.
mitigation_and_workaround: Short term: Enable parsing-shim on identity-proxy that detects JSON array strings and emits one group claim per entry. Applied to a single shard for canary. Workaround for affected users: temporary local RBAC mapping via manual group grant in admin console (requires admin action).
resolution: In progress - patch PR (github.com/redwood/identity-proxy/pull/486) implements robust claim normalization including JSON-array parsing, CSV-splitting, and multiple-claim merging. Plan: run canary for 24h in prod-us-east, then roll to 100% with a feature flag toggled. Post-deploy follow-up: add automated test for claim formats and update runbook doc.
follow_up_tasks: Merge PR and roll out claim-normalization to all identity-proxy shards
Add unit/integration tests for JSON-blob, CSV, and multi-claim scenarios
Notify partner IdP to coordinate attribute schema and document supported formats
Update runbook with troubleshooting steps and sample assertion payloads
